audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Elihu's speech on righteousness, benefit/harm, oppression cries, songs in the night, unanswered prayer, and Job's alleged empty speech. Marked as Elihu's speech, not final theology.

verses.restored: Do you think this is justice? You say, My righteousness is more than the Divine's.

familiar.text: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God’s?

verses.restored: For you say, What benefit is it to you? What profit do I have more than if I had sinned?

familiar.text: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?

verses.restored: I will answer you with words, and your friends with you.

familiar.text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

verses.restored: Look toward the heavens and see; behold the clouds, which are higher than you.

familiar.text: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.

verses.restored: If you sin, what do you do against him? If your transgressions multiply, what do you do to him?

familiar.text: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

verses.restored: If you are righteous, what do you give him, or what does he receive from your hand?

familiar.text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

verses.restored: Your harm affects a person like yourself, and your righteousness a human being.

familiar.text: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.

verses.restored: Because of many oppressions people cry out; they cry for help because of the arm of the great.

familiar.text: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

verses.restored: But no one says, Where is the Divine my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

familiar.text: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

verses.restored: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?

familiar.text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

verses.restored: There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evil people.

familiar.text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

verses.restored: Surely emptiness the Divine will not hear, and Shaddai will not regard it.

familiar.text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

verses.restored: How much less when you say you do not behold him; the case is before him, and you must wait for him.

familiar.text: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.

verses.restored: But now, because his anger has not punished, and he does not greatly regard transgression,

familiar.text: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:

verses.restored: Job opens his mouth in emptiness; without knowledge he multiplies words.

familiar.text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.
